Next steps I propose:
- You review the attached addendum PDF (short) and the benchmarking worksheet.

3) Failure tolerance & credits: we need clear crediting language for missed SLOs (preferably financial credits applied to monthly invoice).

Also we’ll need the final addendum to reference our PO number and the renewal term (12 months).

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity increase — reserved pool throughput addendum

Hi Alicia — thanks for the questions; summary below and attached a short benchmarking worksheet that maps our telemetry to your metrics.

1) tokens/sec definition:
- We measure tokens after tokenizer normalization (BPE) and include assistant/system tokens generated by the model. We report both client-submitted prompt tokens and response tokens; the SLO is expressed as aggregate generated+consumed tokens/sec across the reserved pool.

2) measurement window:
- Default SLO calc: 90th percentile over a 30-day rolling window (UTC). However for initial ramp we can run a 7-day rolling evaluation for the first 60 days and target weekly checks as you requested. I’ve added a ramp schedule in the worksheet.

3) crediting for missed SLOs:
- Proposed credit schedule (subject to legal):
  - If measured throughput falls below 90% of the guaranteed tokens/sec for >12 cumulative hours in the measurement window, CloudFin receives a 5% service credit applied to that month’s Dedicated fee.
  - If below 75% for >12 cumulative hours, CloudFin receives a 15% credit.
  - Credits are capped at 30% per month.

Attachment: Throughput_Benchmarking_worksheet.xlsx (see sheet 'SLO-metrics')

I’ve also included a sample PromQL snippet in the worksheet for how to calculate tokens/sec from our exported metrics (tokens_generated_total / window_seconds).

If this looks acceptable I can convert the bullet items into conversational SLO language for the addendum (objective + remedies + ramp). Hiro — can you propose formal legal phrasing around credits and exceptions (force majeure, scheduled maintenance)?

Thanks,
Rishi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@cloudfin.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudFin Contracts <contracts@cloudfin.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity increase — reserved pool throughput addendum

Alicia — attaching proposed SLO/legal paragraph below for inclusion in the addendum. Happy to iterate.

Proposed SLO language (draft):
"Redwood guarantees that, for the duration of the Agreement Addendum, the Dedicated Reserved Pool assigned to Customer (16 A100 GPUs) will provide a sustained aggregate throughput of 250,000 tokens per second (tokens/sec) measured as the 90th percentile over a rolling 30-day window during Customer business hours (08:00–20:00 PT). Redwood will calculate tokens/sec using the tokenizer-normalized token counts emitted and consumed by the model runtime.

Should Redwood fail to meet the guaranteed throughput for more than twelve (12) cumulative hours in a 30-day measurement window as defined above, Customer is entitled to service credits applied to the Dedicated monthly fee: (a) five percent (5%) if measured throughput is below ninety percent (90%) of the guarantee; (b) fifteen percent (15%) if below seventy-five percent (75%); credits are capped at thirty percent (30%) per monthly billing period. Credits shall not apply during periods of scheduled maintenance (notified at least 48 hours in advance), third-party cloud provider outages, or other force majeure events.

The parties may adopt a 60-day ramp schedule upon commencement of the addendum during which Redwood will perform weekly reporting and apply a seven (7) day rolling evaluation for the initial sixty (60) days.
"

Please review and let us know if any redlines are required. Once we have agreement on wording, Marissa will attach this to the renewal quote and I can coordinate with finance/legal to finalize the addendum.

Regards,
Hiro Tanaka
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
